tier_reason: The README table (OpenCV old ns/op against SSE2 new ns/op, eight rows) matches the record exactly, and the harness is public (sse2/benchmarks_opencv_test.go: opencv.Smooth CV_GAUSSIAN/CV_BLUR/CV_MEDIAN against SimdSse2GaussianBlur3x3, MeanFilter3x3 and median kernels), but CPU model, Go version, OpenCV build flags and the Resolution value are not stated, so first-party C.

corrections.caveats: This is effectively evidence for the C++ Simd library (ermig1979/Simd, compiled by clang and translated to Go assembly by c2goasm) against a 2017-era OpenCV 2.4 cvSmooth path, not a claim about Go; the Go side only calls generated assembly. Image size (the Resolution constant), CPU, Go version and OpenCV build are unstated; Resolution is only a commented-out 'const Resolution = 2048' in sse2/benchmarks_opencv_test.go and was not found in benchmarks_test.go, SimdUtil.go or the GaussianBlur and Median test files. OpenCVSetup only calls opencv.CreateImage, so the OpenCV source images are never filled with test data (the filters timed are largely data-independent, so this probably does not change the result). The OpenCV rows are cgo calls through go-opencv, so a small per-call cgo cost is part of the baseline, though the smallest timed row is 16,623 ns so it is probably minor; OpenCV 2.x is long superseded and newer releases likely have faster SIMD paths for these filters (not measured here), so the ratios may not hold today. First-party numbers, no repeat counts.

notes: Numbers and metadata (136 stars, Apache-2.0, last commit 2017-04-20, abandoned) check out. The speed comes entirely from ermig1979/Simd, which is already listed (wave 10, id https://github.com/ermig1979/simd); per the wrapped-library rule this should be recorded as a duplicate of that entry rather than a Go language win. Shortcomings: no CPU, Go version, OpenCV flags or image size; OpenCV 2.4.10 baseline is stale; OpenCV input images never initialised.

tier_reason: Upgraded C to B: the timings come from an independent party (the authors of the competing tool Sassy) in the evals artifact of their paper, which the catalog's Sassy entry records as published in Bioinformatics (May 2026); the evals README gives exact commands for both tools but no CPU model or compiler flags, so not A. Ish's own peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics Advances, Nov 2025) also claims parity-or-better against parasail, but that was seen only in a search snippet.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Sassy evals README (written by the authors of a competing tool, evals artifact of the Sassy paper): ish takes 69 s with an SSE build and 110 s with the AVX2 build; parasail_aligner with ish's cost parameters (-X 2 -M 2 -o 3 -e 1) takes '81s-198s' across the four striped variants (sse41_128_8, sse41_128_16, avx2_256_8, avx2_256_16); with parasail's default cost parameters it takes '53-69s'. Best against best at matched costs: 81 s / 69 s = 1.17x faster (derived from page data); the per-variant mapping of times is not given. The ish paper (Bioinformatics Advances, November 2025, DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf292) states that ish's core algorithms meet or exceed the performance of their reference implementations in Parasail for both SIMD and GPU alignment as measured by GCUPS (snippet only; paper not opened). The ish README itself gives no performance numbers.
corrections.caveats: The ish paper was published in Bioinformatics Advances (November 2025, DOI 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf292, PMC12930471; seen in a search snippet only) but could not be opened (bioRxiv, doi.org and ncbi.nlm.nih.gov are unreachable here), so the authors' own GCUPS numbers, hardware and build flags are unseen; the only numbers found are from the Sassy repo, where Sassy's authors time ish and parasail as side baselines. CPU model, Mojo and parasail build flags and run count are not given in that README ('For me, this takes 69s for SSE'). The win depends on cost parameters: parasail with its default costs (53-69 s) is as fast as or faster than ish (69 s SSE, 110 s AVX2); at matched costs the best margin is only 1.17x and the mapping of the 81-198 s range onto the four parasail variants is not given. The ish AVX2 build is slower than SSE for this short pattern. The repo ships a reproducible harness (benchmarking/bench_scripts/bench.py, 'pixi run bench-all-cpu', uniprot_sprot 2015_11 and the parasail paper's query set, parasail built with autoreconf and configure; it runs parasail_aligner single-threaded with -x, gap open 3 and extend 1, Blosum62 by default and the saturation-checking 'sat' variants by default) but no stored results and no hardware record. Both sides run Farrar-style striped semi-global alignment, so the comparison is same-algorithm; the mechanism behind ish's edge is not stated in the sources opened. No ksw2 comparison found.

notes: Metadata checks out (63 stars, Apache-2.0, no releases, last commit 2025-10-31, Sassy-tested commit 92f4fad dated 2025-07-21). Upgraded to B on the independent Sassy measurement; shortcomings: marginal 1.17x win only at ish's cost parameters, parasail at default costs ties or wins, no CPU or flags in the README, ish paper numbers unseen. Sassy itself is already listed in wave 14 (a different project, not a duplicate).
